newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe to focus campaign more on jobs.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe to focus campaign more on jobs.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Friday he aimed to focus the election campaign more on jobs and brushed aside opinion polls showing the left-wing opposition almost neck-and-neck with his centre-right coalition.

"Unemployment should be at the heart of the campaign," he told France 3 television. Juppe, deeply unpopular among voters, has come under fire from political allies over a lacklustre campaign for the May 25-June 1 vote.
"What I deeply desire is for the campaign to change tone," he said. "Over the past two weeks it has largely consisted of personal attacks and partisan jibes. The time for such behaviour is over."

The opposition has accused Juppe of giving the campaign an aggressive edge by saying at the outset it would be both "joyful and brutal". Unemployment in France is running at 12.8 percent, a post-war record.

Asked about opinion polls showing the Socialist-led opposition had risen to within striking distance of victory, Juppe said: "That merely proves that there are many people who still have to make up their minds".
"That encourages us to continue the campaign and to do it on the basis of precise proposals," he said.
He said opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin had failed to answer questions such as how he would pay for the creation of 700,000 jobs, one of the left's main promises.
Former prime minister Edouard Balladur said on Friday he would not add to criticisms of Juppe in the ruling coalition and urged a shift to more free-market policies after the vote.

"I think that the head of the government has a difficult role, that he is carrying it out with courage," Balladur told France 2 television. "Don't count on me to add to the chorus of personal criticisms."

Ex-president Valery Giscard d'Estaing stung Juppe's leadership on Wednesday by saying he wanted France to shift to bolder and simpler policies and hinted that President Jacques Chirac should not reappoint Juppe.
Chirac called the vote last month, saying France needed a "new elan", partly to help it join a single European currency from a position of strength.
